blocks.zh: 導論、背景與範圍
blocks.en: Introduction, Background and Scope

blocks.zh: 本章學習目標
blocks.en: Learning Objectives

blocks.zh: 說明本指引的法規地位，並正確解讀「should」與強制性規定的差異
blocks.en: Explain the regulatory status of this guidance and correctly interpret the difference between "should" and mandatory requirements

blocks.zh: 辨識無菌製程 (Aseptic Processing) 與最終滅菌 (Terminal Sterilization) 的技術差異及其風險意涵
blocks.en: Identify the technical differences between aseptic processing and terminal sterilization, and the risk implications of each

blocks.zh: 列舉適用本指引的法規框架（21 CFR parts 210, 211, 600–680）
blocks.en: List the regulatory framework that applies to this guidance (21 CFR parts 210, 211, 600-680)

blocks.zh: 解釋為何無菌製程所需環境控制遠比最終滅菌嚴格
blocks.en: Explain why aseptic processing requires far stricter environmental control than terminal sterilization

blocks.zh: 理解本指引涵蓋的更新主題，並連結至 CDMO 實務操作
blocks.en: Understand the topics updated in this guidance and link them to CDMO operational practice

blocks.zh: 說明無菌製程「最後手段」原則的業務意涵
blocks.en: Explain the business implications of the principle that aseptic processing is a "last resort"

blocks.zh: Section I — Introduction 導論
blocks.en: Section I — Introduction

blocks.zh: 原文內容 Original Text
blocks.en: Original Text

blocks.zh: 導師解析 Tutorial Commentary
blocks.en: Tutorial Commentary

blocks.zh: 核心概念：這份指引是什麼？
blocks.en: Core Concept: What Is This Guidance?

blocks.zh: 本文件是 FDA 在 2004 年發布的正式指引，取代了舊版的 1987 年無菌製程指引。 它的核心目的是協助廠商理解 FDA 對 無菌製程 (Aseptic Processing) 的現行期望，並對應到 CGMP (現行良好製造規範) 法規條文（21 CFR parts 210 和 211）的具體要求。
blocks.en: This document is a formal guidance issued by FDA in 2004, replacing the earlier 1987 aseptic processing guideline. Its core purpose is to help manufacturers understand FDA's current expectations for aseptic processing and how they map to the specific requirements of the CGMP (current good manufacturing practice) regulations (21 CFR parts 210 and 211).

blocks.zh:
對 CDMO 而言，這是接受客戶委託生產無菌製劑時，必須熟讀的基礎文件。
                    無論客戶的品牌藥（NDA）、學名藥（ANDA）、或生物製劑（BLA），
                    本指引都是稽核與技術評估的共同語言。
blocks.en: For a CDMO, this is a foundational document that must be thoroughly understood when accepting contracts to manufacture sterile products. Whether the client's product is a brand-name drug (NDA), a generic (ANDA) or a biologic (BLA), this guidance is the common language for audits and technical assessments.

blocks.zh: 類比：「Should」vs 強制要求——紅綠燈 vs 建議路線
blocks.en: Analogy: "Should" vs. a Mandatory Requirement - Traffic Lights vs. a Suggested Route

blocks.zh: 想像你開車出門：紅燈是法律強制規定，違反就會被罰； 而導航 app 給你的「建議路線」雖然不強制，但若你偏離，出了事情就得自己解釋。
blocks.en: Imagine driving somewhere: a red light is a legal requirement, and running it gets you fined. The "suggested route" from your navigation app is not mandatory, but if you deviate and something goes wrong, you have to explain yourself.

blocks.zh: FDA 指引中的「should」正是建議路線的概念—— 技術上不強制，但若你選擇不遵循，稽核時你必須能提出同等效果的替代做法， 否則 FDA 查廠時很可能將其列為缺失。 換句話說，對有經驗的 CDMO 而言，「should」在實務上幾乎等於「must」。
blocks.en: The word "should" in FDA guidance works like that suggested route. It is not technically mandatory, but if you choose not to follow it, you must be able to show an alternative approach of equivalent effect during an inspection. Otherwise FDA is likely to cite it as a deficiency. In other words, for an experienced CDMO, "should" is in practice almost the same as "must".

blocks.zh: 注意：法規文字箱 (CFR Text Boxes) 的意義
blocks.en: Note: What the CFR Text Boxes Mean

blocks.zh: 本指引內嵌的 CFR 文字箱（法規原文方框）是刻意設計的提醒裝置。 當你看到 CFR 文字箱時，代表接下來的內容已從「建議」升格為 21 CFR 強制規定，具法律效力。 閱讀本指引時，務必區分一般段落（建議性）與 CFR 文字箱（強制性）的不同層級。
blocks.en: The CFR text boxes (boxed excerpts of regulatory text) embedded in this guidance are a deliberate reminder device. When you see a CFR text box, the content that follows has moved from "recommendation" to a mandatory 21 CFR requirement with the force of law. When reading this guidance, be sure to distinguish between ordinary paragraphs (advisory) and CFR text boxes (mandatory).

blocks.zh: 思考練習 Practice Questions
blocks.en: Practice Questions

blocks.zh: 本指引取代了哪一年的舊版無菌製程指引？這代表什麼時代背景的改變？
blocks.en: Which year's earlier aseptic processing guideline did this guidance replace? What change in the surrounding context does this reflect?

blocks.zh: NDA、ANDA、BLA 分別代表什麼類型的藥品申請？請各舉一個例子。
blocks.en: What types of drug applications do NDA, ANDA and BLA stand for? Give one example of each.

blocks.zh: 若 FDA 指引中寫的是「shall」而非「should」，其法律意涵有何不同？
blocks.en: If an FDA guidance said "shall" instead of "should", how would the legal implication differ?

blocks.zh: 身為 CDMO 的 QA 主管，當客戶問「這是 FDA 要求還是只是建議？」，你該如何回應？
blocks.en: As the QA head of a CDMO, how would you respond when a client asks, "Is this an FDA requirement or just a recommendation?"

blocks.zh: CDMO 業務應用場景
blocks.en: CDMO Business Application

blocks.zh: 當客戶在技術轉移會議中主張某項做法「FDA 又沒有強制規定，不需要做」， 你的技術團隊需要能夠清楚說明：雖然指引中使用「should」， 但這代表 FDA 的現行期望 (current thinking)， 若不遵循且無充分科學佐證，稽核時將面臨 483 觀察項目或 Warning Letter 風險。 這不只是法規立場，更是保護雙方商業利益的關鍵溝通能力。
blocks.en: When a client argues in a technology transfer meeting that a certain practice "is not mandated by FDA, so we don't need to do it", your technical team must be able to explain clearly that, although the guidance uses "should", it represents FDA's current thinking. If you do not follow it and have no sound scientific justification, you risk a Form 483 observation or a Warning Letter at inspection. This is not just a regulatory position; it is a key communication skill that protects the commercial interests of both parties.

blocks.zh: Section II-A — Background: Regulatory Framework 背景：法規框架
blocks.en: Section II-A — Background: Regulatory Framework

blocks.zh: 核心概念：法規層次架構
blocks.en: Core Concept: The Regulatory Hierarchy

blocks.zh: 美國對無菌藥品的監管採取「雙軌並行」的法規架構：
blocks.en: The United States regulates sterile drug products through a "dual-track" regulatory framework:

blocks.zh: 21 CFR parts 210 & 211：適用於所有藥品的 CGMP 基礎規定，包含廠房設施、設備確效、製程控制、品管等通用要求。
blocks.en: 21 CFR parts 210 & 211: the foundational CGMP requirements for all drug products, covering general requirements such as facilities, equipment qualification, process controls and quality control.

blocks.zh: 21 CFR parts 600–680：專門針對生物製劑（如疫苗、血液製品、基因治療）的額外要求，由 CBER 監管。
blocks.en: 21 CFR parts 600-680: additional requirements specific to biological products (such as vaccines, blood products and gene therapies), overseen by CBER.

blocks.zh:
一般小分子無菌針劑主要適用 210/211；生物製劑（如 mAb 注射劑）則需同時符合兩套法規。
                    身為 CDMO，接不同類型客戶委託時，要確認適用的法規範疇，才能正確規劃 GMP 策略。
blocks.en: Conventional small-molecule sterile injectables are mainly subject to parts 210/211, whereas biologics (such as mAb injectables) must comply with both sets of regulations. As a CDMO, when accepting projects from different types of clients, you must confirm which regulatory scope applies in order to plan your GMP strategy correctly.

blocks.zh: 類比：法規層次如同建築法規
blocks.en: Analogy: The Regulatory Hierarchy Is Like Building Codes

blocks.zh:
21 CFR 210/211 就像城市通用的「建築基準法」，所有建築物都要遵守；
                    而 21 CFR 600–680 就像針對醫院或核電廠的「特殊建築附加規範」，
                    在一般標準之上額外要求更高規格。
                    若你的 CDMO 同時承接一般注射劑與生物製劑，就等於在同一棟廠房裡同時遵守兩套建築法規，
                    設計與管理的複雜度自然更高。
blocks.en: 21 CFR 210/211 is like the city's general "building code" that every building must follow, while 21 CFR 600-680 is like the "special supplementary code" for hospitals or nuclear plants, which demands higher specifications on top of the general standard. If your CDMO takes on both conventional injectables and biologics, it is like complying with two building codes in the same facility, so the design and management are naturally more complex.

blocks.zh: 注意：CDER vs CBER 的監管分工
blocks.en: Note: The CDER vs. CBER Division of Oversight

blocks.zh: FDA 內部，CDER（藥品評估研究中心）負責監管大多數藥品（含生物類似藥）， CBER（生物製劑評估研究中心）則監管疫苗、血液製品及部分細胞/基因治療產品。 CDMO 在規劃稽核應對與文件策略時，需確認客戶產品的主管機關是哪一個中心。
blocks.en: Within FDA, CDER (Center for Drug Evaluation and Research) regulates most drug products (including biosimilars), while CBER (Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research) regulates vaccines, blood products and some cell and gene therapy products. When planning inspection readiness and documentation strategy, a CDMO needs to confirm which center is responsible for the client's product.

blocks.zh: 若客戶委託你生產一款 mRNA 疫苗，應同時符合哪些 CFR 規定？
blocks.en: If a client commissions you to manufacture an mRNA vaccine, which CFR requirements must you comply with?

blocks.zh: 21 CFR 211 中有哪些條文與無菌製程的廠房設計最直接相關？（提示：211.42, 211.46）
blocks.en: Which provisions of 21 CFR 211 are most directly relevant to the facility design of aseptic processing? (Hint: 211.42, 211.46)

blocks.zh: CDER 與 CBER 的監管範疇如何劃分？請各舉一種產品為例。
blocks.en: How is the regulatory scope divided between CDER and CBER? Give one example product for each.

blocks.zh: Section II-B — Background: Technical Framework 背景：技術框架
blocks.en: Section II-B — Background: Technical Framework

blocks.zh: 類比：兩種滅菌策略的直覺理解
blocks.en: Analogy: An Intuitive Picture of the Two Sterilization Strategies

blocks.zh: 最終滅菌 (Terminal Sterilization) 就像外科醫師使用完手術器械後，將整包器械送進高壓蒸汽鍋滅菌—— 操作過程不需要無塵室，因為最終整包一起高溫殺菌，風險由滅菌步驟統一消除。
blocks.en: Terminal sterilization is like a surgeon who, after finishing an operation, puts the whole pack of instruments into an autoclave. No cleanroom is needed for the handling itself, because the whole pack is sterilized by heat at the end and the risk is eliminated by that single step.

blocks.zh: 無菌製程 (Aseptic Processing) 則像外科醫師在手術前先對每一件器械個別滅菌， 然後在超潔淨的手術室內小心組裝—— 每一個動作、每一個人員、每一次開關艙門都是潛在的污染風險， 全程需要極致的環境控制與操作紀律。
blocks.en: Aseptic processing is like a surgeon who sterilizes each instrument individually before the operation and then carefully assembles them in an ultra-clean operating room. Every movement, every person and every opening of a door is a potential source of contamination, so the whole process demands extreme environmental control and operational discipline.

blocks.zh: 哪個方式更安全？當然是最終滅菌。因此 FDA 明確表示： 只有當最終滅菌不可行時，才使用無菌製程。
blocks.en: Which approach is safer? Terminal sterilization, of course. That is why FDA states explicitly: use aseptic processing only when terminal sterilization is not feasible.

blocks.zh: 核心概念：無菌製程的三個分流滅菌路徑
blocks.en: Core Concept: Three Separate Sterilization Paths in Aseptic Processing

blocks.zh: 由於最終容器無法進行滅菌，每個組成要素必須走自己的滅菌路徑：
blocks.en: Because the final container cannot be sterilized, each component must follow its own sterilization path:

blocks.zh: 玻璃容器 (Glass Containers)：乾熱滅菌 (Dry Heat) — 高溫烘箱，同時去除熱原 (Depyrogenation)
blocks.en: Glass containers: dry heat sterilization in a high-temperature oven, which also removes pyrogens (depyrogenation)

blocks.zh: 橡膠塞 (Rubber Closures)：濕熱滅菌 (Moist Heat / Autoclaving) — 蒸汽高壓，確保高度無菌保證水準
blocks.en: Rubber closures: moist heat sterilization (autoclaving) with pressurized steam, ensuring a high sterility assurance level

blocks.zh: 液體藥品 (Liquid Dosage Forms)：過濾滅菌 (Filtration) — 通過 0.22 µm 除菌過濾器去除微生物
blocks.en: Liquid dosage forms: sterilizing filtration through a 0.22 µm sterilizing-grade filter to remove microorganisms

blocks.zh:
三條路徑匯流於無菌填充間 (Aseptic Fill Room)，在 ISO 5（A/B 級）環境下完成最終組裝。
                    每一條路徑都必須獨立驗證，任何一個環節失效，無菌保證即受威脅。
blocks.en: The three paths converge in the aseptic fill room, where final assembly takes place in an ISO 5 (grade A/B) environment. Each path must be validated independently, and the failure of any one step threatens sterility assurance.

blocks.zh: 重要警示：1980–2000 年的召回教訓
blocks.en: Important Warning: Lessons from Recalls in 1980-2000

blocks.zh: FDA 特別指出，1980–2000 年間因無菌保證不足而召回的產品中， 絕大多數均為無菌製程生產。這個歷史數據不是偶然—— 它深刻反映了無菌製程固有的高複雜度與高風險性。
blocks.en: FDA specifically points out that, among products recalled between 1980 and 2000 because of inadequate sterility assurance, the great majority were produced by aseptic processing. This historical data is no coincidence; it reflects the inherent complexity and high risk of aseptic processing.

blocks.zh: 對 CDMO 而言，這個數據意味著：無菌製程的 GMP 系統必須建立在 預防性設計而非事後補救的基礎上。 一旦召回，不僅是客戶的損失，更是 CDMO 商譽的重大打擊。
blocks.en: For a CDMO, this means the GMP system for aseptic processing must be built on preventive design rather than after-the-fact remediation. A recall is not only a loss for the client, but also a major blow to the CDMO's reputation.

blocks.zh: 為什麼橡膠塞用濕熱而非乾熱滅菌？乾熱對橡膠塞有什麼潛在問題？
blocks.en: Why are rubber closures sterilized by moist heat rather than dry heat? What potential problems does dry heat cause for rubber closures?

blocks.zh: 過濾滅菌 (Filtration) 的原理是什麼？0.22 µm 孔徑能去除病毒嗎？
blocks.en: What is the principle of sterilizing filtration? Can a 0.22 µm pore size remove viruses?

blocks.zh: 若一款蛋白質注射劑因高溫會降解，你的滅菌策略應如何設計？
blocks.en: If a protein injectable degrades at high temperature, how should your sterilization strategy be designed?

blocks.zh: 請列舉三個在無菌填充過程中「任何操作都是潛在污染風險」的具體情境。
blocks.en: List three specific situations in aseptic filling in which "any operation is a potential contamination risk".

blocks.zh: SAL（無菌保證水準）是什麼？SAL ≤ 10⁻⁶ 代表什麼意義？
blocks.en: What is SAL (sterility assurance level)? What does SAL ≤ 10⁻⁶ mean?

blocks.zh:
當 CDMO 業務團隊向客戶介紹無菌製造能力時，最常被問到的問題是：
                    「你們能做最終滅菌嗎？」這個問題背後有深刻的商業邏輯——
                    客戶知道最終滅菌的無菌保證更高、召回風險更低、法規稽核壓力更小。
blocks.en: When a CDMO business team presents its aseptic manufacturing capabilities to clients, the most frequently asked question is: "Can you do terminal sterilization?" There is a sound commercial logic behind this question: clients know that terminal sterilization offers higher sterility assurance, lower recall risk and less regulatory inspection pressure.

blocks.zh:
若 CDMO 只有無菌製程能力，必須能清楚說明：
                    (1) 為何該品項不適合最終滅菌（如蛋白質熱穩定性問題）；
                    (2) 你的無菌製程如何透過環境控制、工藝設計、媒體填充模擬試驗 (Media Fill) 等手段補償這個固有風險。
                    這是技術銷售的關鍵說服點。
blocks.en: If a CDMO has only aseptic processing capability, it must be able to explain clearly: (1) why the product is not suitable for terminal sterilization (for example, thermal stability of a protein); and (2) how its aseptic process compensates for this inherent risk through environmental control, process design and media fill (aseptic process simulation). This is a key persuasion point in technical selling.

blocks.zh: Section III — Scope 範圍
blocks.en: Section III — Scope

blocks.zh: 核心概念：本指引的六大更新主題
blocks.en: Core Concept: The Six Updated Topic Areas of This Guidance

blocks.zh:
相較於 1987 年舊版，本指引針對以下六大領域進行了系統性更新，
                    每一項都對應到 CDMO 日常 GMP 管理的重要模組：
blocks.en: Compared with the 1987 edition, this guidance systematically updates the following six areas, each of which corresponds to an important module of day-to-day CDMO GMP management:

blocks.zh: 人員資格確認 (Personnel Qualification)：gowning 評估、無菌技術訓練、行為控制
blocks.en: Personnel Qualification: gowning evaluation, aseptic technique training, behavioral controls

blocks.zh: 潔淨室設計 (Cleanroom Design)：HVAC 系統、氣流型式、壓差梯度、潔淨室分級
blocks.en: Cleanroom Design: HVAC systems, airflow patterns, pressure differentials, cleanroom classification

blocks.zh: 製程設計 (Process Design)：填充工藝設計、人員動線、設備配置風險評估
blocks.en: Process Design: fill process design, personnel flow, equipment layout risk assessment

blocks.zh: 品質控制 (Quality Control)：無菌測試、培養基模擬填充 (Media Fill)、過濾完整性
blocks.en: Quality Control: sterility testing, media fill (process simulation), filter integrity

blocks.zh: 環境監控 (Environmental Monitoring)：微粒計數、微生物取樣、趨勢分析
blocks.en: Environmental Monitoring: particle counts, microbiological sampling, trend analysis

blocks.zh: 生產記錄審查 (Production Records Review)：批次記錄完整性、異常事件調查
blocks.en: Production Records Review: batch record completeness, investigation of abnormal events

blocks.zh: 這六大主題構成了本指引後續各章節的核心架構。後面的學習都圍繞這些主題展開。
blocks.en: These six topics form the core structure of the sections that follow, and the rest of the learning revolves around them.

blocks.zh: 重要原則：無菌製程是「最後手段」
blocks.en: Key Principle: Aseptic Processing Is a "Last Resort"

blocks.zh: FDA 明確強調：當最終滅菌不可行時，才使用無菌製程。 這不只是技術建議，而是貫穿整份指引的設計哲學。
blocks.en: FDA emphasizes explicitly: use aseptic processing only when terminal sterilization is not feasible. This is not just a technical recommendation; it is a design philosophy that runs through the entire guidance.

blocks.zh: 實際上，對許多蛋白質藥物、脂質體、mRNA 製劑而言， 高溫滅菌會破壞活性成分，最終滅菌確實不可行。 但 FDA 要求廠商必須事先評估並記錄「為何無法採用最終滅菌」， 不能未經評估就直接採用無菌製程。這個評估是 CDMO 技術方案文件的必要組成。
blocks.en: In practice, for many protein drugs, liposomes and mRNA products, high-temperature sterilization would destroy the active ingredient, so terminal sterilization is genuinely not feasible. However, FDA requires manufacturers to evaluate and document in advance why terminal sterilization cannot be used, and not to adopt aseptic processing without that evaluation. This evaluation is a required part of a CDMO's technical proposal documentation.

blocks.zh: 類比：雙腔室注射器的特殊地位
blocks.en: Analogy: The Special Status of Dual-Chamber Syringes

blocks.zh:
雙腔室注射器 (Dual-Chamber Syringes) 是一個有趣的特例——
                    就像「夾心餅乾」一樣，兩種成分分開存放，使用前才混合。
                    這種設計從包裝結構上就使最終滅菌不可行，因為兩腔的成分可能對滅菌條件有不同承受能力。
blocks.en: Dual-chamber syringes are an interesting special case. Like a sandwich cookie, two components are stored separately and mixed only before use. This design makes terminal sterilization infeasible by the very structure of the package, because the components in the two chambers may tolerate sterilization conditions differently.

blocks.zh: 對這類特殊包裝，FDA 並非完全不允許，而是要求廠商探索 輔助加工步驟 (Adjunct Processing Steps)—— 例如對局部可耐受滅菌的組件仍盡可能進行最終滅菌， 以在整體上增強無菌保證水準。這體現了 FDA 風險導向的監管思維。
blocks.en: For such special packaging, FDA does not prohibit it outright, but expects manufacturers to explore adjunct processing steps. For example, components that can tolerate sterilization should still be terminally sterilized wherever possible, to strengthen the overall sterility assurance level. This reflects FDA's risk-based regulatory thinking.

blocks.zh: 隔離器 (Isolator) 的出現：新時代的無菌屏障技術
blocks.en: The Emergence of Isolators: A New Generation of Aseptic Barrier Technology

blocks.zh: 1987 年的舊版指引中，隔離器技術尚未成熟。 2004 年版本特別將隔離器 (Isolator)納入討論， 因為它提供了比傳統潔淨室更高的人員-環境隔離水準—— 操作者完全在隔離屏障之外，透過手套箱 (Glove Box) 操作， 大幅降低人員帶入污染的風險。
blocks.en: In the 1987 guideline, isolator technology was not yet mature. The 2004 version specifically brings the isolator into the discussion, because it provides a higher level of separation between personnel and the environment than a conventional cleanroom: the operator stays entirely outside the barrier and works through glove ports (a glove box), greatly reducing the risk of contamination introduced by personnel.

blocks.zh:
隔離器技術現已成為業界提升無菌保證的重要工具，
                    後續章節將有專節討論其設計與確效要求。
blocks.en: Isolator technology has now become an important tool for improving sterility assurance in the industry, and later sections discuss its design and qualification requirements in dedicated sections.

blocks.zh: 本指引明確「不涵蓋」最終滅菌的相關要求，那麼最終滅菌應參考哪些其他 FDA 文件？
blocks.en: This guidance explicitly does not cover requirements for terminal sterilization. Which other FDA documents should be consulted for terminal sterilization?

blocks.zh: 若你的 CDMO 要承接一款新的蛋白質注射劑，如何向 FDA 說明為何採用無菌製程而非最終滅菌？
blocks.en: If your CDMO takes on a new protein injectable, how would you explain to FDA why aseptic processing was used rather than terminal sterilization?

blocks.zh: 雙腔室注射器所需的「輔助加工步驟」可能包含哪些具體措施？請試著列舉 2–3 項。
blocks.en: What specific measures might the "adjunct processing steps" for dual-chamber syringes include? Try to list 2-3.

blocks.zh: 隔離器 (Isolator) 與傳統潔淨室 (Cleanroom) 在無菌保證設計上的根本差異是什麼？
blocks.en: What is the fundamental difference in sterility assurance design between an isolator and a conventional cleanroom?

blocks.zh: 環境監控 (Environmental Monitoring) 與品質控制 (Quality Control) 在功能上有何不同？可以互相取代嗎？
blocks.en: How do environmental monitoring and quality control differ in function? Can one replace the other?

blocks.zh: 當 CDMO 接受新客戶技術評估時，了解本指引的「範圍聲明」有重要的業務含義：
blocks.en: When a CDMO undergoes a technical assessment by a new client, understanding the scope statement of this guidance has important business implications:

blocks.zh: (1) 能力評估對應：本指引的六大更新主題，正好是 FDA 稽核時最關注的六個領域， 也是 CDMO 能力展示的核心清單。業務開發時，這六個面向的能力証明文件是贏得客戶信任的關鍵。
blocks.en: (1) Capability assessment mapping: The six updated topics of this guidance are exactly the six areas FDA pays most attention to during inspections, and they form the core checklist for demonstrating CDMO capability. In business development, documented evidence of capability in these six areas is the key to winning client trust.

blocks.zh: (2) 可行性評估責任：「最終滅菌不可行才使用無菌製程」這一原則， 意味著 CDMO 在接受委託前，需協助客戶記錄並確認此一評估。 若日後 FDA 稽核時發現此評估付之闕如，委託方與受託方可能共同面臨責任風險。
blocks.en: (2) Responsibility for the feasibility assessment: The principle that aseptic processing is used only when terminal sterilization is not feasible means that, before accepting a project, the CDMO needs to help the client document and confirm this assessment. If FDA finds at a later inspection that the assessment is missing, the sponsor and the contract manufacturer may both face liability risk.

blocks.zh: (3) 隔離器投資決策：對考慮升級無菌製造設施的 CDMO， 隔離器技術的引入不只是技術問題，更是差異化競爭策略—— 能夠吸引對無菌保證要求最嚴格的高階客戶（如細胞療法、高毒性藥物）。
blocks.en: (3) Isolator investment decision: For a CDMO considering an upgrade of its aseptic manufacturing facility, introducing isolator technology is not only a technical matter but also a differentiation strategy, since it can attract high-end clients with the strictest sterility assurance requirements (such as cell therapy and highly potent drugs).

blocks.zh: 本節重點回顧 Section Summary
blocks.en: Section Summary

blocks.zh: 法規地位：本指引取代 1987 年版，幫助廠商理解 FDA 對無菌製程的現行期望；指引中的「should」表示建議而非強制，但實務上等同業界標準。
blocks.en: Regulatory status: This guidance replaces the 1987 edition and helps manufacturers understand FDA's current expectations for aseptic processing; "should" in the guidance means a recommendation rather than a requirement, but in practice it is equivalent to an industry standard.

blocks.zh: 法規框架：無菌製程 CGMP 的主要法規依據為 21 CFR 210 & 211；生物製劑另需符合 21 CFR 600–680；CFR 文字箱代表強制性規定。
blocks.en: Regulatory framework: The main regulatory basis for aseptic processing CGMP is 21 CFR 210 & 211; biologics must additionally comply with 21 CFR 600-680; CFR text boxes denote mandatory requirements.

blocks.zh: 最終滅菌 vs 無菌製程：最終滅菌的無菌保證更高、變數更少；無菌製程需對藥品、容器、塞子分別滅菌，再於高潔淨度環境下組裝，召回風險歷史上較高。
blocks.en: Terminal sterilization vs. aseptic processing: Terminal sterilization gives higher sterility assurance and fewer variables; aseptic processing requires separate sterilization of the drug product, container and closure, followed by assembly in a high-cleanliness environment, and has historically carried a higher recall risk.

blocks.zh: 三條滅菌路徑：玻璃容器（乾熱）、橡膠塞（濕熱/高壓蒸汽）、液態製劑（過濾滅菌），每條路徑均需獨立驗證。
blocks.en: Three sterilization paths: glass containers (dry heat), rubber closures (moist heat/autoclave), liquid formulations (sterilizing filtration); each path requires independent validation.

blocks.zh: 核心原則：無菌製程是「最後手段」——只有當最終滅菌不可行時才使用；廠商需記錄此評估依據。
blocks.en: Core principle: Aseptic processing is a "last resort", used only when terminal sterilization is not feasible; manufacturers must document the basis for this assessment.

blocks.zh: 本指引涵蓋：人員資格確認、潔淨室設計、製程設計、品質控制、環境監控、生產記錄審查六大主題，以及隔離器技術；不涵蓋最終滅菌。
blocks.en: This guidance covers: six topics (personnel qualification, cleanroom design, process design, quality control, environmental monitoring and production records review), plus isolator technology; it does not cover terminal sterilization.

blocks.zh: CDMO 含義：了解以上框架有助於技術能力展示、新品項可行性評估、設施升級決策，以及稽核風險管理。
blocks.en: CDMO implications: Understanding this framework supports capability demonstration, feasibility assessment of new products, facility upgrade decisions and inspection risk management.
